messages:
alex: Quick sync — should we standardize internal surfaces on gRPC and put an Envoy gateway in front for external REST? Thinking about quotas, telemetry propagation, and private-deploy fallbacks.

maria: gRPC is nice but JSON over HTTP is way easier for console/debugging and for partners. :thinking:

tim: gRPC gives typed contracts, streaming, smaller wire overhead. Plus proto evolution is manageable with rules. But yeah, gateway adds operational surface.

azara: Important question: where do we enforce quotas and routing policies? Gateway centralizes that, but we lose per-service context unless we forward metadata.

sam: For private deployments (VPC / on-prem) some customers won't run our Envoy. We need a fallback shim that accepts HTTP and converts to gRPC, or a small sidecar that exposes the same HTTP surface.

maria: Sidecar pattern avoids a central gateway but duplicates policy code across services. Rollouts/patching that policy gets hairy.

tim: If we do gateway + shim, we get single place for rate limiting and auth. But we must be careful: proto -> JSON mapping for API users must be stable.

azara: Also telemetry: we must propagate trace/span ids, tenant id, cost-center metadata. For gRPC it's metadata; for HTTP it's headers. Envoy can map headers <-> metadata but config is nontrivial. Example mapping we sketched:
```
http header -> grpc metadata
X-Request-Id -> x-request-id
X-Tenant -> x-tenant
Authorization: Bearer <token> -> :authority? (validate in gateway)
```

alex: Good. Another constraint: quota granularity. We need token-level accounting (per-api-key) and route/model-level buckets. Gateway can do token accounting cheaply, but we'd still want service-side counters for double-checking.

sam: For private deployments without gateway, the shim must emit the same accounting events to our metrics endpoint (or write locally to a metrics agent). That implies an SDK + integration tests.

maria: Can we avoid per-service duplication by publishing a tiny policy library and an Envoy config snippet customers can apply? Then private deployments either run Envoy or the library.

tim: Ops: deployments and rollouts matter. If policy is in gateway, we can canary changes there. If in sidecars, every service needs the update before the policy is changed. Gateway looks easier for iteration.

azara: One more: error surface. If gateway drops metadata or fails mapping, downstream will see opaque errors. We need clear fallthrough semantics and test harness.

alex: Proposal: run a 2-week spike PoC. Build: 1) a minimal HTTP->gRPC shim lib (node + go) that maps headers->metadata and emits billing/telemetry events; 2) an Envoy config that demonstrates header<->metadata mapping + rate limit filter; 3) an integration test that simulates Dedicated + Private (no Envoy).

assignments: tim + zara = PoC impl; maria = console dev for JSON mapping + UX notes; alex = write RFC + rollout plan; sam = metrics/agent integration.

alex: I'll open the RFC/draft and a short checklist. Link to draft: https://rfc.internal/adapter-spike (WIP).

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployed api-adapter-spike:v0.1 -> 5% traffic to dedicated-test cluster :rocket:

maria: Sounds reasonable. If PoC shows mapping edge cases, we'll evaluate sidecar vs gateway tradeoffs for RCF. :thumbsup:

tim: Ok starting spike tomorrow. Quick note: let's log all header->metadata mappings and add unit tests for proto JSON marshalling.

azara: I'll add telemetry integration tests and a small chaos script to drop headers and make sure errors are surfaced cleanly.

sam: Also add a small script to replay usage events for quota verification.

alex: Great — we'll sync next Wed for spike status. Thanks everyone.
